provisions.summary: Repeals the scheduled standard deduction increases for tax years after 2027, 2029 and 2030 (to $18,000/$13,500/$9,000, then $20,000/$15,000/$10,000, then $24,000/$18,000/$12,000). The standard deduction stays at the 2026 amounts: $16,000 joint, $12,000 head of household, $8,000 single or separate.
provisions.quote: [(G) For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2027: (i) $18,000 in the case of a joint return

provisions.summary: Repeals the bracketed schedules for taxable years after 2026 and after 2028 in all three filing-status tables. The schedule for taxable years after December 31, 2024 stays in force for 2027-2031 (top rate 11% over $650,000 joint, $487,500 head of household, $325,000 single).

provisions.summary: Child and dependent care credit: replaces the AGI-banded applicable percentage (25% down to 15%) with 50% reduced by one point per $3,000 of AGI over $150,000, with a floor of 15%.
provisions.quote: equal to fifty per cent reduced by one percentage point for each $3,000, or fraction thereof, by which the taxpayer's adjusted gross income exceeds $150,000

provisions.summary: Child and dependent care credit: adds a disallowance period of ten taxable years after a final decision that a claim was due to fraud, and two taxable years after a final decision disallowing a claim.
provisions.quote: No credit shall be allowed under this section for any taxable year in the disallowance period.

provisions.summary: Child and dependent care credit: defines adjusted gross income as federal AGI under the Internal Revenue Code.
provisions.quote: adjusted gross income as defined by the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.

provisions.summary: Extends the sunset of Act 163, SLH 2023 from December 31, 2027 to December 31, 2032. The earned income credit stays at 40% of the federal credit and the larger food/excise credit table stays in place through 2031. The sunset also covers Act 163's child and dependent care credit changes (sections 235-55.6(c) and the related credit sections).
provisions.quote: provided that on December 31, [2027,] 2032, this Act shall be repealed

notes: Sections 1 and 2 hold the 2026 standard deduction and the tax-years-after-2024 bracket schedule fixed through 2031; neither changes anything for 2027 itself relative to the stated 2026 amounts, but the bracketed 2027 and 2029 schedules would otherwise have applied. Section 3's child and dependent care credit changes cannot be modeled and apply from tax year 2027 (section 6). The sunset extension in section 4 runs to December 31, 2032, past the 2027-2031 window; section 3 is likewise repealed and reenacted in its prior form on that date. The Act 163 credit extensions (EITC 40%, food/excise table) take effect for tax year 2028, since the current-law sunset is after 2027. The bill is an introduced by-request draft with a blank introducer line. Capital gains treatment, itemized deductions and the personal exemption are not touched.
